title: Budget exhaustion — a human gate — is invisible in `tp summary` and the HEADLINE; the plain-text surface says 'no action required' while the run is blocked on the human
scenario: taskplane/README.md declares a budget-exhausted contract 'a human gate ... never auto-released'. dashboard.widget() detects it (dashboard.py:~2108, with a comment admitting 'without this the banner reads no action needed while the run is actually blocked') — but the fix was applied only to the rich widget. user_summary (loop.py:2261-2318) and headline_loop (dashboard.py:2060-2076) never read the meter. skills/taskplane/SKILL.md states 'The plain-text summary is always sufficient to operate the loop', and on Codex/Tag it is the primary surface. Concrete failure: an execute contract hits max_actions mid-wave; `tp summary` prints 'In progress — 1/3 task(s) settled ... no action required — agents are working under the harness' indefinitely; the user waits on a run that is waiting on them.
fix: Port the widget's budget_exhausted detection (contract budget.max_actions vs .taskplane/meter.json) into user_summary — set decision='Grant more actions (tp budget --grant N) or clear the contract' and headline='Blocked — action budget exhausted' — and append a '· BLOCKED: budget exhausted' marker to headline_loop.

title: track.py re-derives the loop-state directory and breaks the documented per-user-state invariant on team plans
scenario: docs/state-spec.md (lines 101-113) and loop._state_dir (loop.py:42-56) rule that loop.json/tracks.json stay in the PRIVATE external store even on a team plan, with TASKPLANE_STORE=repo as the ONLY exception. track._state_dir instead uses tp.kb_root(ws), which follows get_mode(): on a team/enterprise plan (committed .taskplane-kb/config.json, no env var) it resolves to the in-repo store. Result: `tp track switch` archives/restores a loop.json under .taskplane-kb/knowledge/state/ that loop.load() never reads (it reads external_store/knowledge/state/loop.json), so switching tracks silently does nothing to the live loop — two tracks then share one state machine, and per-user in-flight state (tracks.json, archived loops) gets committed with the code, exactly what the spec forbids.
fix: Make loop._state_dir the single owner of the rule: export it (drop the underscore or add loop.state_dir()) and have track.py import and call it instead of re-deriving via tp.kb_root. Add a test that, with a shared config.json present and no TASKPLANE_STORE, track._live_loop(ws) == loop._loop_path(ws).

title: next_action performs unlocked read-modify-write saves — the same lost-update class the H2 fix closed in gate()
scenario: gate() applies transitions under mutate() to a fresh read precisely because wave workers update loop.json concurrently (H2 comment, loop.py:1595-1600). But next_action loads state at line 558 and later calls bare save(ws, state) at line 610 (flipping built→evaluate in parallel mode) and again at 645 (design rebaseline) with no lock and no re-read. Two wave workers finish near-simultaneously: worker A's `loop gate --task tA` marks tA built under the lock; the driver's concurrent `loop next` (which loaded state before A's gate) saves its stale snapshot — tA reverts from built to running and its _submission is wiped. tA's worker has already exited, so nothing ever re-gates it: the wave stalls with a task permanently 'running' until a human hand-edits loop.json.
fix: Wrap the two mutating sections of next_action in `with mutate(ws) as st:` and re-derive the built list / fingerprint check from the locked fresh state (the rest of next_action is read-only and can keep using an unlocked load).

title: Engine still owns rendering/publishing; loop↔dashboard is a latent import cycle and loop.py's next extraction seam is evidence validation + the dashboard decorator
scenario: dashboard.py imports loop at module top (dashboard.py:18); loop imports dashboard only lazily inside _with_dashboard (loop.py:2387) and _publish_artifacts (2358). The layering doc says the view derives from engine read models, yet the engine calls the view on every gate/submit/next/approve and copies artifacts itself. The cycle is one refactor away from an ImportError: anyone lifting `import dashboard as _dash` to loop's header (the natural cleanup) breaks module import for every entry point. Meanwhile loop.py sits at 2421 lines mixing the state machine with ~250 lines of evidence validation (_evaluation_errors/_engineering_review_errors/_task_dod_errors/_signoff_dod, lines 1057-1266, 1698-1734) and ~90 lines of publishing/rendering (2330-2420) that gate() only consumes as error lists.
fix: Extract evidence.py (the four *_errors validators + _submission_staleness — pure functions over ws/state, mirroring the design_contract.py extraction) and move _with_dashboard/_publish_artifacts wrapping into the CLI/driver layer (tp.cmd_loop wraps the results), so loop.py never imports dashboard in any form and drops toward ~1,800 lines of pure state machine.

title: Corrupt state files crash with bare tracebacks - inconsistent with the codebase's own fail-closed handling
scenario: loop.load() (loop.py:161-162), track._registry (track.py:38-39), kb.load_index (kb.py:40-41) and requirements.load_index (requirements.py:53-54) all call json.load with no error handling. The codebase elsewhere treats exactly this case deliberately: load_active returns None, _meter_load raises typed MeterCorrupt, kb._load_index_at has strict/lenient modes, design_contract.read_json returns structured errors. A truncated loop.json (e.g. after a crash of the non-atomic writers above, or a hand edit) makes EVERY command - `tp loop status`, `tp summary`, `tp context`, the dashboard - die with an uncaught JSONDecodeError and no remediation hint, stalling the loop with no path forward.
fix: Give loop.load/track._registry/kb.load_index/requirements.load_index the read_json treatment: catch (OSError, ValueError) and return a structured error naming the corrupt file and the remedy (restore from the artifacts snapshot or re-init), consistent with _meter_load's fail-closed pattern.

title: flock fallback silently degrades to NO locking — exactly on the FUSE/network filesystems this plugin explicitly targets
scenario: loop.mutate (loop.py:197-204), kb.mutate (kb.py:71-77) and tp._file_lock (taskplane_lite.py:1191-1206) all do `except (ImportError, OSError): pass`. On FUSE-mounted sandboxes (the environment safe_remove exists for — taskplane_lite.py:1090) and on NFS/SMB mounts, fcntl.flock commonly raises ENOTSUP/ENOLCK — so the wave serialization mutate() exists to provide silently vanishes: two wave workers gate concurrently, the second save clobbers the first, a gated task reverts to 'running' and the wave stalls (the exact failure documented at loop.py:1420-1423). Nothing is traced or printed when the degradation happens, so the operator cannot know their waves are unserialized. On Windows (fcntl ImportError) the same holds for every store.
fix: On flock failure, fall back to an mkdir-based lock (atomic on FUSE/NFS/Windows) with a bounded wait; at minimum tp.trace(ws, 'lock_degraded', path=...) once per process so the degradation is visible in the trace.

title: Three severity vocabularies with lossy mappings across the findings contract — a 'blocker' or 'major' finding passes the EM gate, 'critical' renders as medium
scenario: Producers and consumers of findings.json disagree on the severity enum: the lens-agent brief mandates high|med|low (lens.py:364), every lenses/*.md verdict schema mandates blocker|major|minor|question|praise, and the tp-engineering skill uses {severity,...} freely. The EM gate blocks sign-off only for severity in ('critical','high') (loop.py:1260), and the dashboard maps blocker→high but leaves major AND critical falling through to 'med' (dashboard.py:513-514). Concrete failure: an EM review that merges per-lens outputs written in the catalog's own vocabulary records an unresolved {'severity':'blocker'} finding — _engineering_review_errors raises no error, `loop gate pass` succeeds, and the human is offered sign-off over an open blocker; conversely a 'critical' finding is displayed as a medium chip in the headline the human decides from.
fix: Define one canonical enum plus a normalization map in the kernel (e.g. tp.normalize_severity: blocker/critical→high, major/medium→med, minor→low, question/praise→info) and call it at both consumption points — loop._engineering_review_errors and dashboard._SEV_KEY — then align lens.py's brief text and lenses/_generate_lens_prompts.py to the canonical set.

title: loop init over an in-flight loop silently discards all progress
scenario: With a loop at step=evaluate (task passed, evidence gathered) in /tmp/qa2-serial, re-running `tp loop init "<same goal>"` returned {"initialized": true, "step": "pm"} and reset step, tasks, approvals and baseline with no refusal, no --force requirement, and no archived-state note. One mistyped init destroys a governed session's state machine.
fix: Refuse when a non-terminal loop exists ('active loop at step=X — pass --force to restart or `loop resolve abort` first'), or archive the prior state file with a visible 'previous loop archived to …' in the response.

title: Design-introduced contracts have no sanctioned path into the graph before plan DoR requires them recorded
scenario: A design legitimately proposes a NEW boundary, e.g. contract:order-cancelled-v2, not declared on the requirement (only requirement contracts are auto-recorded — at `tp req new` (tp.py:981) and at the plan gate's apply pass, loop.py:1033-1040). design_plan_errors forces the planner to carry the id onto a task; depgraph.readiness then blocks: 'contracts are not recorded in the dependency graph' (depgraph.py:805-809). The designer is forbidden to mutate the graph (agents/tp-designer.md:18) and the planner's contract has no Bash tool (loop.py:274), so neither governed role can run `tp graph edge` — the flagship Design→Plan flow stalls with no in-band remedy or documented recovery.
fix: At the plan gate's apply=True pass, record design/task-declared contract nodes the same way requirement contracts are recorded (req→contract edge or bare node registration); alternatively require design contracts ⊆ requirement contracts at Design DoD so the gap cannot arise.

title: v2.2.1 attestation-warning branch is only half-pinned: warning payload, trace event, and signoff variant untested
scenario: test_v140_tag.py:129-131 asserts only `by == "(unattributed)"` at plan_approval. Nothing asserts out["warning"] (attached at loop.py:1938-1939), the `loop_approve_unattributed` trace (loop.py:1853), or the signoff-gate arm of the `step in ("plan_approval", "signoff")` condition (loop.py:1845). Deleting lines 1938-1939 or the trace call, or dropping "signoff" from the tuple, leaves all 477 tests green — the release-noted 'warned, not silently equivalent' behavior can regress silently.
fix: Extend the v140 test (or add to test_v221_fixes.py) to assert out["warning"] contains 'without --by', assert the loop_approve_unattributed trace event exists, and add a twin test parked at signoff.

title: track._state_dir duplicates loop._state_dir with divergent resolution - track switch can archive the wrong loop.json
scenario: loop._state_dir (loop.py:43-60) resolves external-store state with an explicit legacy fallback: it uses <ws>/knowledge/state when a legacy loop.json exists there and the external one does not. track._state_dir (track.py:21-23) instead uses tp.kb_root(ws)/state, which prefers the external knowledge dir whenever that DIRECTORY exists - regardless of where loop.json lives. On a partially-migrated project (external knowledge/ dir created by kb writes, loop state still at legacy <ws>/knowledge/state/loop.json), `tp track switch` looks for the live loop at the external path, finds nothing ('has_loop_state': false), archives nothing - and the next track silently inherits the previous track's live loop state instead of getting a fresh one.
fix: Delete track._state_dir and import loop._state_dir (or hoist one shared resolver into taskplane_lite) so track archiving and the engine always agree on where loop.json lives. Also make track._save atomic like loop.save.

title: Track registry (tracks.json) is written non-atomically and read with an unguarded json.load — a torn write loses ALL track metadata
scenario: `_save` (line 42-45) does `open(_reg_path,'w')` then `json.dump` — truncate-then-write, no temp+replace. If the process is interrupted (crash, SIGKILL, full disk) mid-write, tracks.json is left empty or half-written. `_registry` (line 34-39) then calls `json.load` with NO try/except, so every subsequent `tp track new/list/switch/close` raises an uncaught ValueError and crashes. Because `switch()`/`close()` also shutil.move the live loop.json into `tracks/<name>/` keyed off this registry, a lost/corrupt registry strands the archived loop.json files and drops the active-track pointer — the user's multi-track loop state becomes unrecoverable. This diverges from the project's own established safety pattern: kb._save_index (kb.py:45) and loop.save (loop.py:173) both already use temp+os.replace with the explicit comment 'a reader never sees a torn index'.
fix: Write tracks.json via `tmp = path+f'.tmp.{os.getpid()}'; json.dump(...); os.replace(tmp, path)` exactly as kb._save_index/loop.save do, and make `_registry` tolerate a corrupt file (catch ValueError → treat as needing repair / keep a `.bak`) instead of an unguarded json.load.

title: gate()'s final staleness re-attest runs outside the mutate() lock, leaving a TOCTOU window before the transition commits
scenario: The re-attest at lines 1585-1590 recomputes the workspace fingerprint, then tp.clear(act_ws) at 1592 removes the contract (workspace now ungoverned), and only then does the locked transition begin at 1602 — which re-checks the step but not the fingerprint. A process that modifies the evaluated files in that gap (an eager fixer agent, a human editor, a merge) gets its changes blessed by a gate whose evidence was attested against different bytes; the single-writer guarantee the submission fingerprint exists to provide has a hole exactly at the commit point.
fix: Move the final _submission_staleness check inside the `with mutate(ws)` block (it is a cheap hash compare relative to the validation already done), and clear the contract after the locked transition rather than before.

title: On Codex hosts 'cheap' resolves to inherit and the brief does not say so — planned cost routing silently has zero effect
scenario: _default_tier_models() maps cheap→None on Codex (taskplane_lite.py:1173-1178), so a planner marking simple tasks '"model": "cheap"' in tasks.json ships briefs with model:null and every dispatch inherits the full session model — the plan's intended cost reduction never materializes. The resolved routing is surfaced only in `tp onboard --json`'s model_tiers (tp.py:175-176), which a mid-project operator never re-reads; the brief itself (loop.py:829-841) carries model:null with no hint that setting TASKPLANE_MODEL_CHEAP would activate the saving.
fix: When model_for_tier() returns None for a non-'standard' requested tier, include a one-line note in the brief (e.g. "tier 'cheap' resolves to inherit — set TASKPLANE_MODEL_CHEAP to route this cheaper") so the routing gap is visible at the moment it costs money.

title: EM gate refusal 'engineering review does not recommend sign-off' doesn't name the field that encodes the recommendation
scenario: EM gate in /tmp/qa2-serial with complete lens coverage, impact and tests evidence still fails with only 'engineering review does not recommend sign-off'; the required meta.gate.verdict = "pass"|"recommend-pass" in .em-review/findings.json (checked at loop.py:1251-1252) is discoverable only from source.
fix: Extend the message: 'set meta.gate.verdict to "pass" or "recommend-pass" in .em-review/findings.json'.

title: gate --task with an unknown task id is misdiagnosed as missing worker evidence
scenario: Parallel wave in /tmp/qa2-par with ta submitted: `tp loop gate pass --task zz` (no such task) returns 'worker evidence was not submitted — the worker must run loop submit pass|fail'. The stated next action (submit) cannot succeed for a nonexistent task; the actual fault (unknown id) is never named, unlike submit which validates --task (v2.2.1 H1).
fix: Validate the gate's --task against wave members first and return 'unknown task id zz — wave members: ta, tb', mirroring the H1 submit-side validation.

title: claim() holds the global loop lock across git subprocesses, serializing parallel wave startup
scenario: claim() enters `with mutate(ws)` and, while holding the exclusive flock on loop.json.lock, runs tp.git_head(agent_ws) and tp.dor_check(...) — which shells out to `git status --porcelain` (is_dirty) in the worktree. On a large repo a cold git status takes 1-3s per worktree. When the orchestrator dispatches a 10-task wave and all workers claim concurrently, they serialize behind the lock: wave startup takes 10-30s of dead time instead of ~2s, and the window in which a concurrent submit/gate blocks on the same lock widens accordingly.
fix: Run git_head + dor_check BEFORE acquiring the lock (they read the worker's own worktree, not shared state) and keep only the read-check-write of the task's status/workspace inside mutate(); re-verify the status is still claimable after locking.

title: Gate-snapshot artifacts grow without bound: HEADLINES.md is read in full per gate and graph.json is re-copied per transition
scenario: _publish_artifacts runs on every successful gate/submit/next/approve. It reads ALL of HEADLINES.md just to inspect the last line (line 2364: open(p).read().rstrip().splitlines()) before appending — O(file) per gate on an append-forever file, so a long-running team store pays quadratic cumulative reads — and dumps the full graph (json.dump(g, indent=1), line 2355-2356) into artifacts/<slug>/graph.json every time, which on a large repo copies megabytes per transition into a store that is committed on team plans. artifacts/<slug>/ dirs also accumulate one per goal forever with no pruning, and init()/onboard list them all.
fix: Read only the tail of HEADLINES.md (seek(-4096, SEEK_END)) and cap it (e.g. keep last 500 lines); write graph.json to the artifacts snapshot only when the graph fingerprint changed since the last publish (compare meta.content_fingerprint against the copy).

title: design_rebaseline trace event is asserted by no test
scenario: test_v221_fixes.py:136-150 pins that a stale design_graph_fingerprint is re-captured (H3), but no test greps the trace for the `design_rebaseline` event with old/new prefixes written at loop.py:641-644. Renaming or removing the trace — the audit artifact that distinguishes a legitimate rebaseline from silent fingerprint drift — fails nothing.
fix: In TestH3DesignRebaseline, read .taskplane/trace.jsonl after the rescan and assert one design_rebaseline event with old=="stale-fp"[:12] and new==current fingerprint prefix.

title: H2 carry-over covers only tasks: ab/parallel/selection-reset/graph_dor plan-gate fields unpinned under concurrency
scenario: TestH2LockedGateTransition pins tasks preservation at evaluate and the step-moved refusal, but the plan-gate carry-over block (loop.py:1616-1624: ab flag, parallel flag, round-scoped selection pop, graph_dor) has no concurrent-mutation test. A regression that, e.g., stops popping stale `selection` or drops the recomputed graph_dor when applying the fresh-read state passes the whole suite, re-opening the exact clobber class H2 fixed.
fix: Add a plan-gate twin of test_gate_preserves_concurrent_worker_update that mutates state mid-validation and asserts ab/parallel/graph_dor come from the validation snapshot while a stale selection key is removed.

title: tracks.json written non-atomically and track switch moves loop.json without a lock
scenario: _save (track.py:42-45) truncate-writes tracks.json; switch() (track.py:76-93) does two shutil.move calls plus a registry save with no lock. A crash between archiving the current track's loop.json and saving the registry leaves the live loop stranded under tracks/<name>/ with 'active' still pointing at the old track — the next `tp loop status` reports no loop and a re-init would orphan the archived state.
fix: Write tracks.json via tmp+os.replace and take loop's mutate() lock (the loop.json.lock already exists) across switch/close so registry and file moves can't interleave with a live gate.
